questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Angles and Magnitudes
questions.problem: Suppose $|\,p\,|=\sqrt{3}$ and the angle between vectors $p$ and $q$ is $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Find the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =|\,p\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.problem: Let $a=⟨3,-1,-1⟩$ and $b=⟨4,4,2⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,q\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{q}_{x}^{2}+{q}_{y}^{2}+{q}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+4\cdot 1+2\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{p}\,q & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,p\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{p}_{x}^{2}+{p}_{y}^{2}+{p}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{25}} \\  & =\frac{9}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p+{\text{comp}}_{p}\,q & =\frac{9}{2}+\frac{9}{5} \\  & =9(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =9(\frac{5}{10}+\frac{2}{10}) \\  & =\frac{63}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

and

$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c-{\text{comp}}_{c}\,d & =\frac{5}{3}-1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$

questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.problem: Let $p=i-3j$ and $q=xi+2j+k.$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =1\cdot x+(-3)\cdot 2+0\cdot 1 \\  & =x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ x-6 & =0 \\ x & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
